correctness.rationale: Proximal stationarity gives a unique fused-hub scalar root and finitely many strict complementarity regimes. On a regime with m active vertices including the hub the residual differential is the one-block centering Q_S=I-P_S; its exact Gini norm follows from binary-level coarea, with j active ones and t outside ones, and equals (m-1)(2n-m)/[m(n-1)]. Maximizing the forward difference 2n/[m(m+1)]-1 gives m(m-1)<=2n<=m(m+1). Strictly feasible KKT active sets for any positive penalties and a single fused-leaf perturbation attain every local norm. The fitted block projector P_S is doubly stochastic and Gini-contractive. This proves finite n>=2, sharp n=4 onset and asymptotic 2-2sqrt(2/n)+O(1/n); a finite cut check alone would not.
